source_text:
Ἀλλ’ ἵνα τῶν ἀρχαίων ὑποδειγμάτων παυσώμεθα, ἔλθωμεν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἔγγιστα γενομένους ἀθλητάς: λάβωμεν τῆς γενεᾶς ἡμῶν τὰ γενναῖα ὑποδείγματα.
διὰ ζῆλον καὶ φθόνον οἱ μέγιστοι καὶ δικαιότατοι στύλοι ἐδιώχθησαν καὶ ἕως θανάτου ἤθλησαν.
λάβωμεν πρὸ ὀφθαλμῶν ἡμῶν τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς ἀποστόλους:
Πέτρον, ὅς διὰ ζῆλον ἄδικον οὐχ ἕνα οὐδὲ δύο, ἀλλὰ πλείονας ὑπήνεγκεν πόνους καὶ οὕτω μαρτυρήσας ἐπορεύθη εἰς τὸν ὀφειλόμενον τόπον τῆς δόξης.
διὰ ζῆλον καὶ ἔριν Παῦλος ὑπομονῆς βραβεῖον ὑπέδειξεν,
ἑπτάκις δεσμὰ φορέσας, φυγαδευθείς, λιθασθείς, κήρυξ γενόμενος ἔν τε τῇ ἀνατολῇ καὶ ἐν τῇ δύσει, τὸ γενναῖον τῆς πίστεως αὐτοῦ κλέος ἔλαβεν,
δικαιοσύνην διδάξας ὅλον τὸν κόσμον, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ τέρμα τῆς δύσεως ἐλθὼν καὶ μαρτυρήσας ἐπὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων, οὕτως ἀπηλλάγη τοῦ κόσμου καὶ εἰς τὸν ἅγιον τόπον ἀνελήμφθη, ὑπομονῆς γενόμενος μέγιστος ὑπογραμμός.
thought_title: From ancient examples to the apostles' contests
orientation: The Roman church has just listed ancient examples of envy's harm and now turns to the recent apostles as models of endurance.
pass_a_gloss: But so that we may cease from the ancient examples, let us come to the athletes who have become nearest; let us take the noble examples of our own generation. Because of envy and spite the greatest and most righteous pillars were persecuted and contended even to death. Let us take before our eyes the good apostles: Peter, who because of unjust envy endured not one nor two but many labors and thus having borne witness went to the due place of glory. Because of envy and strife Paul showed the prize of endurance, having worn chains seven times, having been exiled, having been stoned, having become a herald in both the east and in the west, he received the noble fame of his faith, having taught righteousness to the whole world, and having come to the limit of the west and having borne witness before the rulers, thus he was released from the world and departed to the holy place, having become the greatest pattern of endurance.

choices.why: Keeps the athletic metaphor of contest and struggle that runs through the passage; 'contenders' would lose the concrete image.
Literal rendering of the architectural metaphor for the apostles as supports of the church; 'columns' is weaker.
Keeps the verbal force of μαρτυρέω and its connection to martyrdom without importing the later technical sense 'was martyred'.
Preserves the athletic prize metaphor; 'reward' would flatten the contest imagery.
Literal rendering of the public-office term; 'preacher' would import a later Christian technical sense.
Keeps the sense of a model to be traced or copied; 'example' is acceptable but 'pattern' better captures the underlying metaphor of a writing-copy.

pass_b_english: But let us stop drawing on ancient examples and come to the athletes who lived closest to us. Let us take the noble examples of our own generation.
Because of envy and spite, the greatest and most righteous pillars were persecuted and struggled all the way to death.
Let us set before our eyes the good apostles.
Peter, because of unjust envy, endured not one or two but many hardships, and having borne witness in this way he went to the place of glory that was due him.
Because of envy and strife, Paul showed the prize of endurance.
He wore chains seven times, was exiled, was stoned, became a herald in both the East and the West, and received the noble fame of his faith.

He taught righteousness to the whole world, and when he had reached the boundary of the West and borne witness before the rulers, he was released from the world in this way and was taken up into the holy place, becoming the greatest pattern of endurance.

problems.why: Greek terms may differ, but reader sees varying English pairs.
problems.fix: Note if these translate distinct Greek terms or are stylistic variation.

problems.quote: Paul showed the prize of endurance
problems.why: 'Showed the prize' is odd; should be 'won' or 'received the prize.'
problems.fix: Revise to: 'Paul won the prize of endurance.'

problems.quote: he was released from the world in this way and taken up into the holy place
problems.why: Implies bodily assumption like Elijah; contradicts known tradition of Paul's martyrdom.
problems.fix: Add note: text may mean 'departed to be with God,' not physical assumption.

problems.why: Used interchangeably for people and groups; reader may wonder if 'the elect' is a distinct group from 'the elect of God'.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'the elect of God' or clarify it refers to all believers.

edits.old: Paul showed the prize of endurance.
edits.new: Paul won the prize of endurance.

edits.old: he was released from the world in this way and taken up into the holy place
edits.new: he was released from the world in this way and departed to the holy place

fixed: The 'envy and spite' issue is stylistic variation in the English; the source uses ζῆλον and φθόνον, and 'spite' is an acceptable rendering of φθόνος. No change needed.
The 'elect of God' issue is not present in this passage; no change needed.

problems.quote: Paul won the prize of endurance.
problems.why: ὑπέδειξεν means 'pointed out, showed, displayed', not 'won'. Paul displays or shows the prize of endurance as an example. 'Won' changes the verb's sense and agency.
problems.fix: Because of envy and strife, Paul pointed out the prize of endurance.

edits.old: Because of envy and strife, Paul won the prize of endurance.
edits.new: Because of envy and strife, Paul showed the prize of endurance.

fixed: Fixed 'won' to 'showed': source ὑπέδειξεν means showed/displayed, not won.

problems.why: ἀνελήμφθη means 'was taken up' (passive, by God); 'departed' loses the passive and the ascent.
problems.fix: and was taken up into the holy place

edits.old: and departed to the holy place
edits.new: and was taken up into the holy place

fixed: Fixed 'departed to the holy place' to 'was taken up into the holy place' because ἀνελήμφθη is aorist passive meaning 'was taken up'.
Left 'showed the prize of endurance' unchanged because ὑπέδειξεν means 'showed', not 'won'.

last_rejected.why: Glossary fixes 'envy' for ζῆλος; φθόνον is distinct but 'spite' obscures the paired vices.
last_rejected.ruling: φθόνος commonly means envy/jealousy; 'spite' is within normal range. Paired with ζῆλος, meaning is not lost.
